C-UPDATER-STATS.IntentSummary: Implement the approved update-funnel counters spec in one wave in a dedicated worktree off fork/main: the governed SCRIPT module M-071 mt-stats-gateway (tools/stats-gateway/ — redirect-only Cloudflare Worker with the /feed and /pkg routes, strict OS/platform/semver validation, one aggregate Analytics Engine datapoint per valid request via waitUntil, workers_dev disabled, owner-executed deployment documented in the README; plus query.mjs with dry/live aggregate tables), the two-entry client endpoints array in tauri.conf.json (gateway feed URL with exactly the from/os placeholders first, today's GitHub URL second), the release.yml feed-fragment url fields pointed at the /pkg routes (in-file VERSION + CHANGE_SUMMARY bump there; the strict-JSON config edit recorded in this bundle), the vitest include growth so tests/tools runs under npm test, the two-entry expectation in tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js, and the mark-site privacy-page amendment per R-6 (local repository, deploy separate). Fixed here as the spec deferred: the wrangler route pattern updates.mark.xronocode.com/* with workers_dev = false; query.mjs speaks the Analytics Engine SQL API over GraphQL (owner CF_API_TOKEN); day buckets are UTC. No product code beyond configuration; MAS, rollback paths and the signature scheme untouched; nothing deploys and no release runs from this wave. The plan's own review gate (four corners, two consecutive clean passes — rounds 10-11 of the ReviewLog) completed before approval. Approval basis: the owner instruction of 2026-10-30 (translated from Russian: "1 давай реализуем" — implement the stats change), extending spec R-9's protocol order; execution and the PR follow this approval, deployment stays owner-executed.

T-001.Title: M-071 gateway worker: routes, validation, redirect-only counting

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tools/stats-gateway/worker.mjs with the house MODULE_CONTRACT header (M-071 mt-stats-gateway, SCRIPT + LOCALS): /feed validates GET-only, exactly the from/os parameters, os against {darwin, windows} (the {{target}} substitution) and from against strict semver, then fires one Analytics Engine datapoint (index event=check, blobs day/os/from, UTC day) inside waitUntil and 302-redirects to the GitHub latest.json URL; /pkg/{platform}/{version} validates against the platform table {darwin-aarch64, windows-x86_64} plus strict semver, fires event=pkg (blobs day/platform/version) and 302-redirects to the derived GitHub asset URL; every other method, path, parameter set or value is a plain 404 with zero datapoints and zero redirects; route and platform matching is exact and case-sensitive with no trailing-slash or percent-decoding tolerance; no route ever returns a body it made; Cloudflare edge metadata (request.cf, CF-IPCountry) is never read; worker.mjs emits the BLOCK_STATS_FEED / BLOCK_STATS_PKG log markers on the two counted paths; wrangler.toml carries the updates.mark.xronocode.com/* route, workers_dev = false and the Analytics Engine binding (zone pre-check: the README cites the C-22 fact that the xronocode.com zone is DNS-managed in Cloudflare before any route is deployed).

T-002.Title: Gateway unit pins: derivation table, guards, best-effort counting

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: vitest.config.ts's include grows tests/tools/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts,mjs} FIRST (matching no pre-existing file; coverage include and thresholds untouched) so the new suite is runnable from this task on; tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs (with the house MODULE_CONTRACT header, an M-071 local) pins: the full derivation table (both platforms × version → exact GitHub Location), the os-table vs platform-table separation, 404-with-zero-datapoints for every malformed class (non-GET, missing/extra/garbage parameters, unknown platform, non-strict version, traversal input, trailing slashes, wrong case), zero reflected input in any Location (open-redirect guard), the datapoint shape against a fixture binding, best-effort counting (an absent or erroring binding changes no response — the redirect/404 always returns), and two baseline-true source scans (house precedent: tests/renderer/commands/updater.test.js reads sources): worker.mjs never reads request.cf / CF-IPCountry / user-agent, and src/renderer sources introduce no NEW network-egress or analytics APIs beyond the named baseline allowlist (the spec's delta-form pin: the C-56 remote image-copy fetch in editorWithTabs/editor.vue, blob-URL fetches, and the dormant globally-registered axios client — src/renderer/src/axios/index.js, imported in main.js with zero call sites — are pre-existing and allowed; anything else that initiates network traffic or smells of analytics fails); the suite's remaining static pins (the two-entry endpoints array, both gateway pkg URL prefixes in release.yml, m068's windows_release_base byte-unchanged) are added in T-005 once those edits exist.

tools/stats-gateway/query.mjs (with the house MODULE_CONTRACT header, an M-071 local): dry mode (fixtures inlined in the script, zero network, no fixture files) prints the day × event × OS/platform table and the from-version breakdown; live mode reads only CF_API_TOKEN from the environment and queries the Analytics Engine SQL API printing the same shape; the README documents the owner-executed wrangler deploy steps and route, the C-22 zone fact (the xronocode.com zone is DNS-managed in Cloudflare), the Analytics Engine binding, workers_dev disabled, the success reading (from={N} appearing after N shipped, with the fresh-install caveat), the downloads-vs-clicks reading (plain downloads as the GitHub-counter-derived approximation: asset total minus pkg counts), the three-month retention window and UTC day buckets; no credentials or account identifiers are committed.

tauri.conf.json plugins.updater.endpoints becomes exactly two entries — https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/feed?from={{current_version}}&os={{target}} first, today's GitHub URL second — with the pubkey and installMode byte-unchanged and the mas overlay still shipping no updater; tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js endpoints expectation becomes the same two-entry array (gateway first, GitHub second), with the file's own in-file VERSION bump + CHANGE_SUMMARY entry (governed M-046 local).

C-1.Name: Gateway outage or 5xx
C-1.Situation: The worker is down, rate-limited or erroring during a client's periodic update check.
C-1.Expected: The updater treats the non-2XX as a miss for that entry and continues to the second endpoints entry — the GitHub latest.json — so the check completes exactly as before; auto-checks and manual checks both keep working; the only effect is that the outage window is absent from the counters (undercounting, never breakage).

C-2.Name: Gateway never speaks for the feed
C-2.Situation: Any bug, compromise or misconfiguration of the worker that could affect manifest content.
C-2.Expected: A correct or misconfigured worker cannot affect content: every route is redirect-only — a Location header and no body it made — so the manifest bytes a client parses always come from the redirect target. A COMPROMISED worker controls the Location header and can point anywhere; the honest bound is what can be applied, not where it can point: the pinned minisign key lets only project-signed artifacts install (never arbitrary code), the updater's default version check additionally refuses downgrades, and any anomaly surfaces as from-transition outliers in the counters.

C-3.Name: Not an open redirector
C-3.Situation: Malformed or hostile input: /pkg/../../evil, /pkg/unknown/1.0.0, /feed with garbage parameters, unexpected paths, scanner traffic.
C-3.Expected: Strict validation (platform against the two-entry table, version against strict semver) means every unrecognized input gets a plain 404 with zero datapoints and zero redirects; every Location header ever produced is one of the derived GitHub URLs; nothing from the request appears in any response target.

C-4.Name: Mixed fleet rollout
C-4.Situation: Old clients (pre-config-change) and new clients coexist after the change ships.
C-4.Expected: Old clients keep checking GitHub directly (uncounted) but read whatever latest.json the newest release publishes — so their artifact fetches count at the gateway as soon as the first R-3 manifest ships; new clients' checks count too (R-2 config); coverage grows monotonically with releases and is reported honestly (the README and query tool state which population each number covers).

C-5.Name: Windows split finally exists
C-5.Situation: A Windows user clicks Update in-app; another downloads the installer from the website.
C-5.Expected: The in-app click resolves through /pkg/windows-x86_64/{ver} (counted as a pkg event) while the website link stays the direct GitHub asset (uncounted by us) — the two populations separate by URL construction, replacing today's single mixed counter; the minisignature against the app-pinned key verifies the installer identically on both paths.

C-6.Name: Counting write fails
C-6.Situation: The Analytics Engine binding is absent, throttled, or errors on a request.
C-6.Expected: The response is identical to the healthy case — the datapoint write happens inside waitUntil, its failure is swallowed with a log line, and the redirect still returns; counting is best-effort by contract, and no client ever waits on or notices the datastore.

C-7.Name: Retention window
C-7.Situation: The owner queries numbers older than three months, or wants year-over-year history.
C-7.Expected: The query tool and README state the Analytics Engine three-month retention plainly; day buckets are UTC; queries outside the window return nothing rather than inventing data; long-term storage is a recorded NonGoal (a future export change if the rolling window proves too short) — no data-loss claims are made beyond the window.

C-8.Name: Update success attribution
C-8.Situation: The owner asks how many of the clickers actually landed on the new version.
C-8.Expected: No client code exists for this and none is added: a success is the appearance of from={new version} among later checks (the placeholder carries it); the query tool prints the from-breakdown and the README explains the reading and its honest limits (a user who updates and never launches again is invisible; a fresh site install of N also reports from=N — the pkg and site counters separate the populations).

C-9.Name: Privacy posture unchanged
C-9.Situation: Any user or reviewer asks what Mark now tracks.
C-9.Expected: The app still contains zero analytics and its CSP still forbids renderer egress (pinned by a source scan); the gateway records day-level aggregates (event, OS/platform, version) with no IP, no user agent, no identifiers; the site privacy page says exactly this in the amended disclosure; no cross-session or cross-user correlation is possible from the stored data by construction.

C-10.Name: App Store edition
C-10.Expected: Nothing: the mas overlay strips the updater block entirely, store builds never touch the gateway, and their update story stays the store's own; the privacy-page sentence scopes itself to the download edition.

C-11.Name: Rollback paths untouched
C-11.Situation: A user runs the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK restore while the gateway is in place.
C-11.Expected: The restore behaves exactly as its applied spec pinned: two direct deterministic GitHub fetches, offline on macOS; the gateway neither counts nor intermediates restore traffic, and a gateway outage cannot affect a rollback (recovery never depends on analytics infrastructure).

C-12.Name: Release pipeline discipline
C-12.Situation: The R-3 edit lands in release.yml while releases remain owner-gated.
C-12.Expected: The feed composition changes in code and CI (the build lane stays green; the manifest shape is pinned by the static fragment tests, and the first live proof is the owner-gated release), and no release runs, tags or publishes follow from merging this change; the first real release that carries the new manifest is a separate owner authorization, and until then the feed is byte-identical to today's.
